citation.title: Reinforcement Learning Guided Engineering Design: from Topology Optimization to Advanced Modelling

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For a 10 × 10 grid, GA followed by PPO lowered FE compliance from the GA-only value of 19.3654 to 18.2786, with the two methods described as having comparable wall-clock time.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Separate Appendix comparison: classical ~1 s / PPO ~18 min = 1/1080 on a 5 × 5 grid; equivalently classical was ~1080× faster. This is not the primary outcome.
claim.alternatives: Abstract qualitatively claims a speed and quality improvement over GA alone. Appendix quantitatively compares 5 × 5 PPO and gradient optimization: compliance 33.6 versus 89.63, time ~18 min versus ~1 sec.

baseline.classical_method: Density-based gradient optimization; Python version of 88-line topology optimization code (Appendix)
baseline.implementation: Python topopt_cholmod.py; Appendix command: python3 topopt_cholmod.py 5 5 0.05 1 2 1
baseline.hardware_ml: 2.9 GHz Dual-Core Intel Core i5 for PPO training; Apple M1 Pro for HRL and GA–PPO hybrid (Section 3)
baseline.problem_size: 5 × 5 grid for direct classical/PPO comparison (Appendix); 4 × 4, 6 × 6, 10 × 10 elsewhere (Section 3)
baseline.ml_time: ~18 min wall-clock (Appendix, 5 × 5 PPO; whether training or inference is unclear)
baseline.training_time: ~80 min for 1M PPO steps on 2.9 GHz Dual-Core Intel Core i5 (Section 3); ~32 min PPO refinement following ~1 min GA on Apple M1 Pro (Section 3)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated separately; FE analysis supplies training rewards (Section 2.1)
baseline.quality_gap: PPO compliance 33.6 versus classical 89.63 (Appendix, 5 × 5; lower is better)

R1.evidence: Section 3, p. 9: the primary comparison is FE compliance for GA alone versus GA–PPO at roughly equal wall-clock time; no primary speed ratio is claimed.

R2.evidence: Section 3, p. 9: GA is the primary classical comparator; no protocol R2 failure criterion is established. Appendix separately uses CHOLMOD for a gradient baseline.

R3.evidence: Section 3, p. 9: the primary outcome compares compliance at comparable runtime, without a speed advantage requiring amortization.

R4.evidence: Section 3, p. 9 and Appendix pp. 16–17 report FE-based compliance on returned designs; no aggregate constraint-violation or failed-design rate is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: One explicit classical-versus-PPO comparison on a 5 × 5 grid (Appendix); four grid sizes investigated overall (Section 3)

notes: Publisher PDF was accessible in the web tool, though the local publisher host returned HTTP 523 to fetch.js. Section 3 states the PPO force location differed between training and inference. Section 3/Fig. 3 explicitly labels one HRL example cherry-picked. Code availability declaration names https://github.com/gigatskhondia/gigala. The Appendix benchmark does not distinguish PPO training from inference time.
